title: plane
body:
## plane

Creates a single rectangular quad of width (local X) by height (local Y) in the XY plane, centred on centre, with its normal along +Z. Use it for floors, backdrops and cutting or wrapping sheets; choose grid instead when the surface will be deformed, because a plane has only four vertices.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- A plane has no thickness; add solidify before boolean or STL publication that needs a closed solid.
- The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

Native binding: `plane`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material` | one node | yes | `material` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `width` | Extent of the quad along local X, centred on centre. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"exclusiveMinimum":true}` | `2` |
| `height` | Extent of the quad along local Y, centred on centre. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"exclusiveMinimum":true}` | `2` |
| `centre` | World position [x, y, z] of the plane's centre. Schemaxis assigns it as the object's location, so the mesh itself stays about the local origin and later modifiers that work about that origin (mirror, bend, twist) use this point. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `smoothShading` | When true, every face of the generated plane is marked smooth so Blender interpolates normals and the tessellated surface renders without visible facets; when false the faces render flat. Geometry and vertex positions are identical either way. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` |
